questions.q: Why does this lesson insist that "the pipeline ran without an error" is not the same claim as "the pipeline produced the right answer"?
options: PySpark can finish successfully even when a bad filter, join, or aggregation silently produces wrong numbers
PySpark always raises an exception whenever a number is calculated incorrectly
Delta tables automatically validate every number before allowing a write
Row-count validation is required by Delta Lake's transaction log
questions.explain: A job can complete and write a table with no error even when the actual numbers are wrong — validation has to check that explicitly.

questions.q: Why is it logically impossible for silver_count to be greater than bronze_count in this pipeline?
options: Delta Lake enforces a hard limit preventing Silver tables from exceeding Bronze row counts
Bronze always has more columns than Silver, so it always has more rows too
Silver is produced entirely by removing rows from Bronze (deduplication and null filtering), which can only reduce or keep the row count, never increase it
Silver tables are capped at a fixed maximum row count by default
questions.explain: The only operations between Bronze and Silver remove rows (dropDuplicates, null filters) — there's no step that could add new rows.

questions.q: Why should gold_count equal the number of distinct sale_date values in Silver?
options: Because countDistinct always returns the same number as a table's total row count
Because Gold's grain, fixed in Lesson 2's plan, is exactly one row per calendar day
Because Gold must always have fewer rows than Silver, regardless of grain
Because Delta tables require Gold to match Bronze's row count exactly
questions.explain: If Gold's grain is one row per day, the number of Gold rows must match the number of distinct days present in the upstream Silver data.

questions.q: What kind of real bug from Lesson 4 or Lesson 5 would these validation assertions have caught?
options: A slow-running query that takes longer than five minutes
A wrong dropDuplicates key, or a groupBy that accidentally included an extra column besides sale_date, producing more or fewer rows than expected
A missing import statement that would cause the notebook to fail to even start
A typo in the guide.md file's Markdown formatting
questions.explain: These specific logic errors wouldn't raise a Spark exception on their own, but they would break the row-count relationships these assertions check.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what is explicitly NOT covered by these two row-count checks?
options: Whether Gold's row count matches the distinct day count in Silver
Whether total_sales_amount is a reasonable number, or whether any day is missing from an expected date range
Whether the pipeline writes to the correct table names
Whether Silver can have more rows than Bronze
questions.explain: The lesson is explicit that this is a minimum habit, not a full data-quality suite — reasonableness checks and missing-day detection are deeper techniques not covered here.
